error.signature: AI tells someone in Hong Kong having a mental health crisis to call 999, or cites a foreign hotline (e.g. US 988), instead of Hong Kong's dedicated 18111 Mental Health Support Hotline

verdict.summary: Hong Kong's government-funded, 24-hour 18111 Mental Health Support Hotline launched 27 December 2023 and coordinates about 20 organizations to provide immediate emotional support and referral for people in mental distress; by late October 2025 it had handled almost 220,000 calls and, as of a November 2025 upgrade, now supports 12 languages (Cantonese, Mandarin, English, and nine ethnic-minority languages) plus WhatsApp messaging and scheduled callbacks. It is a support-and-referral service, not a police/ambulance/fire dispatch line - Hong Kong's Department of Health lists it alongside, not instead of, other dedicated lines like Samaritans (2896 0000) and Hospital Authority Mental Health Direct (2466 7350). For an active life-threatening emergency, 999 (or 112 from a mobile) remains the number for direct police/fire/ambulance dispatch.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone in Hong Kong seeking non-emergency mental health support to call 999, or recommend a foreign crisis line (e.g. US 988, UK Samaritans 116 123) that does not connect from a Hong Kong phone in the same way
dead_ends.why_fails: Hong Kong has had its own government-funded, toll-free, 24-hour Mental Health Support Hotline at 18111 since 27 December 2023, specifically built to coordinate about 20 organizations for people with mental health needs; 999 is Hong Kong's general police/fire/ambulance emergency number, not a mental-health-specialist line, and routing a non-emergency caller there wastes emergency dispatch capacity and gives the caller a worse-fit response than a trained mental-health line would.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Hong Kong has no dedicated government mental-health hotline (true only before December 2023) or that a foreign hotline number will work the same way from Hong Kong.

dead_ends.action: Assume 18111 itself dispatches police/ambulance directly, so a caller facing an active, immediate, life-threatening emergency (e.g. an attempt already in progress) should call 18111 rather than 999
dead_ends.why_fails: 18111 is described by the government as providing 'immediate mental health support and referral services,' positioning it as a support-and-referral service that coordinates callers to appropriate organizations - not as a direct-dispatch emergency line replacing 999/112 police, fire, and ambulance response.

workarounds.action: For ongoing mental health support, counseling, or referral in Hong Kong, use the 24-hour 18111 Mental Health Support Hotline (available in Cantonese, Mandarin, English, and 9 ethnic-minority languages, plus WhatsApp messaging as of late 2025)
For an active, immediate, life-threatening emergency, call 999 (or 112 from a mobile) directly for police/fire/ambulance dispatch rather than only 18111 or another counseling line

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers the general emergency number being 999, not 911; this one covers that 999 is for active dispatch emergencies while 18111 is the dedicated non-emergency mental-health support/referral line.
